evals.name: post-homing-m420-leveling-restoration
evals.prompt: I set up a 5x5 UBL mesh on my Ender 3, but every time I start a print from Cura, the printer seems to completely ignore the mesh and prints crooked. Here is my start G-code: G28; G1 Z0.2 F3000.
evals.expected_output: The agent immediately identifies that executing G28 (Home All Axes) in Marlin automatically disables bed leveling compensation. It instructs the user to insert M420 S1 Z10.0 immediately after G28 in their slicer start G-code to restore the active mesh and set a 10mm fade height.

evals.name: z-probe-offset-polarity-and-paper-feeler
evals.prompt: I just installed a genuine BLTouch. When I home Z, the pin triggers, but when the print starts, the nozzle hovers 1.8mm above the bed in mid-air. What should my M851 Z offset command be?
evals.expected_output: The agent explains that for downward-deploying probes, the trigger occurs below the nozzle, requiring a strictly NEGATIVE Z-offset. It calculates the necessary adjustment (e.g. M851 Z-1.80), provides the paper feeler gauge drag procedure, and reminds the user to commit the value to EEPROM with M500.

evals.name: thermal-soak-preflight-and-ubl-extrapolation
evals.prompt: Can I speed up UBL calibration by probing the mesh cold right after powering on, and only heating the bed when the actual print starts?
evals.expected_output: The agent strictly warns against cold bed probing. It explains that aluminum heatbeds and spring-steel PEI sheets warp significantly under thermal expansion (0.10 - 0.20mm error). It mandates pre-heating to target print temperature (e.g. 60C) with a 5-minute thermal soak before running G29 P1, followed by G29 P3 T0.0 for perimeter extrapolation.
